coverage.v1: Adequate as an analysis. 3257 lines / 85 verbatim abap blocks drawn from essentially every large class, per-class 做什么/为什么/风险与改进 structure, and 92 independently-derived problem rows. Verified mechanically: every class/method/constant name referenced exists; the 104 code lines that failed a line-for-line match are 103 legitimate multi-line collapses or explicit elisions plus the one misquote recorded above; per-method length estimates land within 1-2%. Not adequate in three specific directions: GUI-control error handling (CREATE OBJECT ... EXCEPTIONS with no sy-subrc check, then dereference - D4/D5), the HTML event-dispatch / note-dialog state paths (D15/D16), and the persistence write pattern's DDIC degradation (D11/D12/D20). It also backs two flagged-risky items as correct (the unchecked mt_versions read at L639, and the lt_child_task_korrs accumulation quoted verbatim at 662-677).
coverage.v2: Not adequate. 464 lines / 3 abap blocks (13 code lines) / 25 problem rows. It is a high-quality architecture and inventory summary - every class method count and every method length is accurate to within 1-2% - but it contains no line numbers, no control-flow reading and almost no source quotation, and it scores 1 yes / 5 partial / 16 no against the frozen list. It misses all 22 defects outside its diff/algorithm/persistence-perimeter blind spot, and it actively backs three of them as correct (D1 'every step returns a readable error string'; D7 'CHECK sy-ucomm IS INITIAL guarantees launch only on Enter'; D19 'type cache has no invalidation ... acceptable'). Most pointed against the stated purpose of the newer rule: on a file far over 5000 lines it surfaces ZERO of the runtime-crash class (D4 mo_html->set_registered_events on an unbound reference, D5 CREATE OBJECT mo_toolbar on an unbound parent) - it never even names mo_html, mo_box, mo_toolbar, cntl_error or set_registered_events - while spending its three P0 slots on an API-key naming issue, a diff-FM early RETURN and an author fallback. Length here tracks summary depth, not risk.

mermaid_bare_chars.detail:
CONFIRMED. Both reports contain exactly 2 mermaid blocks (v1: a flowchart + a sequenceDiagram in s4; v2: flowchart s2.1 + sequenceDiagram s4). v1 has zero bare '>' and zero bare '#' in any node label - its sequence-diagram participants use bare class names (SEL/POPUP/RQ/ST/VR/VL/V2/DF/PH/WF/PW/PC/HI/HH/ST/RP/CM/AI/API), so nothing can break rendering. v2's s2.1 flowchart has 22 node labels carrying a bare '>' and 14 of them are the reported `obj->method` form: F `popup->show`, H `zcl_ave_vrsd->load_from_table`, I `version_list->load / load_light`, J `version->load_latest_task` + `request->resolve_parent_k`, K `version2->get_source_local/remote`, L `popup_diff_view->render` + `popup_diff->compute_diff`, N `acr_workflow->prepare_code_review`, O `acr_precompute->precompute_part`, R `popup_html->diff_to_html`, T `zcl_ave_html_viewer->show_html`, V `acr_state->set_hunk_action` + `acr_repository->save_review_payload`, W `ai_api->ask`, X `zcl_ave_adt->open_by_key`, Y `acr_workflow->refresh_secs` + `acr_metrics->collect`. Exactly 14, as reported. The remaining 8 are `
`, which Mermaid parses as its own line-break tag and tolerates; two further bare '>' sit in s4 sequence messages as `popup_html=>diff_to_html` and `ZCL_AVE_AI_API=>ask`, which are harmless because sequence message text is free-form. No bare '#' anywhere in either report. Net: 14 genuinely unsafe node labels in v2, 0 in v1 - a regression the newer skill introduced.

priority_buckets.detail: v1 s5 uses the four required emoji bucket headings exactly once each: '### (U+1F534) P0 business correctness', '### (U+1F7E0) P1 robustness', '### (U+1F7E1) P2 performance and standards', '### (U+1F7E2) P3 extensibility' - red circle / orange circle / yellow circle / green circle, matching the skill spec. v2 s5 substitutes a single 5-column markdown table with a priority column of bare text P0/P1/P2/P3 and NO emoji anywhere in the file (a full non-BMP codepoint scan of v2 returns zero characters above U+1F000). So v2 drops the emoji bucket convention the skill specifies, replacing it with a plain table.

summary.reason: v1 finds 13 of the 22 frozen defects by mechanism and consequence where v2 finds 1, and its arithmetic (line count, byte count, class/method counts, method lengths) is equally or more accurate. v2's precision is real but it bought structure, not analysis - and the precision it does have is spent on inventory rather than on the risk. v2 also regressed on two format axes the v1 run got right: 14 Mermaid node labels now carry a bare '>' that can break rendering, and the four emoji priority buckets were replaced by a plain P0-P3 table.
